papers.title: Polysomnographic Sleep in Idiopathic Nightmares: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 case-control studies (7 in meta-analysis, 112 nightmare individuals and 112 controls) found no significant differences in sleep macro-architecture between individuals with idiopathic nightmares and healthy controls. The authors highlight that limited data on sleep micro-architecture and autonomic measures preclude confident conclusions and call for further investigation.

papers.title: Lifespan Trajectories of Resting State Bipolar EEG Power
papers.summary: Lifespan trajectories of resting-state bipolar EEG power were derived from 12,906 observations (ages 12–70) in 5,781 participants without alcohol use disorder, showing sharp power decreases from ages 12 to early 20s followed by divergent patterns across frequency bands and sex differences in inter-frequency correlation trajectories. The differencing procedure in bipolar data appears to reduce global and regional phase synchrony effects, yielding higher inter-frequency correlations than monopolar data.

papers.title: EEG Signatures Support a Shrinking Spotlight of Attention After Errors.
papers.summary: Using EEG in 21 participants during a luminance-varying flanker task, the study found that frontal midline theta power related to increased decision threshold and faster drift rate, but these relationships were not modulated by errors. After errors, the relationship between posterior alpha/beta power and drift rate was enhanced, supporting separate roles for midfrontal control and sensory-specific attentional adjustment.

papers.title: Repeated remimazolam sedation for interstitial brachytherapy in cervical cancer: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 100 cervical cancer patients undergoing repeated interstitial brachytherapy, remimazolam produced fewer intraoperative adverse events than propofol (17.78% vs 59.42%, RR 0.30, p<0.001), including lower respiratory depression and hypotension, with stable sedative requirements across three sessions and no differences in sleep quality.

papers.title: Beyond Snoring, Sleepiness and Surgery: Update on the Prevalent Symptoms of and Treatment Effects in all Age Groups With Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: In a single-center cohort of 489 children with pediatric obstructive sleep apnea, restlessness, chronic insomnia, and kicking legs were more prevalent nocturnal symptoms than snoring, while neurocognitive issues affected 93.7% and improved more with positive airway pressure (94.9%) than with adenotonsillectomy (73.1%), with PAP showing threefold higher odds of neurocognitive improvement after adjustment.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances and Sarcopenia in Older Adults: Clinical Associations, Potential Mechanisms, and Management Strategies.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes observational evidence linking sleep disturbances (abnormal duration, poor quality, insomnia, circadian disruption, obstructive sleep apnea) to sarcopenia in older adults, discusses potential biological and behavioral mechanisms, and outlines management strategies, while highlighting that causality remains uncertain and prospective and randomized trials are needed.

papers.title: Distinct sleep and rest-activity profiles according to adjuvant treatment exposure in women treated for breast cancer.
papers.summary: In an exploratory study of 62 women treated for breast cancer, those receiving chemotherapy plus radio- and endocrine therapy had fewer but longer nocturnal awakenings and shorter sleep-onset latency compared to non-chemotherapy and healthy control groups, while non-chemotherapy patients showed lower rest-activity rhythm robustness. Fatigue was negatively correlated with rest-activity rhythm amplitude in the non-chemotherapy group, suggesting distinct sleep-wake profiles by treatment exposure.

papers.title: Effect of a wearable-based individualised multidomain lifestyle intervention on cognitive and physical function in older adults at risk of decline (INSPIOR): a single-centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a 6-month randomized controlled trial with 355 at-risk older adults, a wearable-based multidomain lifestyle intervention produced a small adjusted between-group difference in MoCA (0.58 points, 95% CI 0.03–1.13; Holm-adjusted p=0.12) that did not survive multiplicity adjustment, with no significant differences in Trail Making Test or skeletal muscle mass index. The intervention was associated with mild skin irritation and dietary-recording stress but no serious adverse events.

papers.title: Modulating stress and sleep through a multi-compound dietary supplement: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
papers.summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial tested morning adaptogens, evening sleep supplements, and their combination in 103 healthy adults over two weeks. Morning ashwagandha and Rhodiola rosea supplementation improved perceived stress, subjective sleep quality, and positive affect compared to placebo, with minimal effects on other outcomes.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic patterns of electroencephalography (EEG)-derived aperiodic activity across schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar, and depressive disorders: A systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 30 studies (N=2298) on EEG-derived aperiodic activity in schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar, and depressive disorders, finding heterogeneous results in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, more consistent flatter slopes and reduced offsets in major depressive and treatment-resistant depression, limited bipolar evidence, and sensitivity to treatment-related modulation. The authors conclude that aperiodic parameters may be more informative as context-sensitive within-subject markers of cortical state and treatment change than as fixed diagnostic signatures.

papers.title: Cognitive impairment in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: A conceptual framework and therapeutic implications.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on cognitive impairment in idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) and proposes a conceptual framework in which cognitive dysfunction arises from interactions among elevated intracranial pressure, cerebral venous hypertension, symptom amplifiers such as chronic headache, sleep disturbance, pulsatile tinnitus, and psychiatric comorbidity, and biological/socioeconomic modifiers. It argues that cognition should be recognized as a clinically meaningful and potentially treatment-responsive outcome in IIH, particularly in patients without papilledema.

papers.title: Understanding sleep-related quality of life in caregivers of people with traumatic brain injury.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a 6-month randomized controlled trial examined associations among subjective and objective sleep-related quality of life, health-related quality of life, and care recipient functioning in 257 informal caregivers of persons with traumatic brain injury. Objectively measured and subjective sleep-related quality of life were weakly correlated; greater between-subjects sleep variability, but not sleep duration, was associated with worse global physical and mental health, while subjective sleep impairment and fatigue were highly correlated and moderately to highly associated with health-related quality of life.

papers.title: Environmental circadian disruption alters rhythmicity of clock and epigenetic gene expression in SKH-1 female mouse livers.
papers.summary: The study measured relative gene expression in female SKH-1 mouse livers under normal and disrupted light schedules to test whether environmental circadian disruption alters rhythmic expression of core clock and epigenetic regulatory genes. Disruption caused significant loss of rhythmic expression in 5 of 8 core clock genes (Cry1, Cry2, Npas2, Nr1d1, Per2), loss of rhythmicity in all active demethylases and Zfp57, and slight damping of Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b rhythmicity.

papers.title: Predicting One-Year CPAP Adherence and Use Trajectories Utilizing Baseline and Early Use Data
papers.summary: The study developed and evaluated models using baseline and early CPAP use data to predict one-year CPAP adherence and use trajectories in CPAP-naive adults with obstructive sleep apnea. Baseline features alone yielded an AUROC of 0.678, while using 7, 14, or 30 days of CPAP data improved AUROCs to 0.787, 0.816, and 0.854; four one-year trajectories were identified, with early CPAP data substantially improving predictive performance for both adherence and trajectory.

papers.title: Potential effect of replacing sedentary behavior with physical activity on the risk of atrial fibrillation: results from the UK Biobank and REGARDS study
papers.summary: Using accelerometry and isotemporal substitution models in 86,096 UK Biobank and 5,777 REGARDS participants free of atrial fibrillation at baseline, this study estimated the effect of replacing 30 minutes of sedentary behavior with physical activity or sleep on incident atrial fibrillation. In fully adjusted models, replacing sedentary behavior with moderate-to-vigorous physical activity was associated with lower atrial fibrillation odds in REGARDS (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.63–1.01) but not in UK Biobank, while light activity and sleep substitutions showed no clear associations.

papers.title: Differences of physical activity, sleep quality and depressive symptoms in patients with diabetes and non-diabetes undergoing maintenance hemodialysis in Xi'an, China: A cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared physical activity, sleep quality, and depressive symptoms between 113 diabetic and 173 non-diabetic patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis in Xi'an, China. Diabetic patients had significantly lower adjusted activity scores, higher Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index global scores, and higher Beck Depression Inventory-II scores than non-diabetic patients; older age and higher BDI-II scores were positively associated with diabetes, while adjusted activity scores and hemodialysis duration were negatively associated.

papers.title: Effects of Perioperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine Spray on Clinical Outcomes of Pulsed Radiofrequency in Patients with Zoster-Associated Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized double-blind trial of 68 patients with zoster-associated pain undergoing pulsed radiofrequency, perioperative intranasal dexmedetomidine spray reduced hemodynamic fluctuations and improved postoperative pain and sleep quality scores compared to saline control, with no severe adverse events.

papers.title: Vanillin alleviates circadian disruption-induced cognitive impairment: involvement of gut microbiota alterations and tryptophan metabolism.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of circadian disruption, oral vanillin improved spatial learning and recognition memory and corrected abnormal tryptophan, kynurenine, and kynurenic acid levels. Vanillin also modulated gut microbiota composition and diversity, enhanced intestinal barrier function and immune homeostasis, and reduced hippocampal astrocyte activation.

papers.title: Boder's dyslexia subtypes as a severity continuum with a definitional route axis - A behavioural companion to harmonised qEEG cross-spectra.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: Behavioral analyses of 520 children with dyslexia found no natural clusters for Boder subtypes; rather, dysphonetic, dyseidetic, and mixed subtypes formed overlapping regions of continuous severity and route distributions. Subtype distinctions were largely definitional, with unknown-word spelling separating dysphonetic from dyseidetic nearly perfectly, and removing the defining variable eliminated residual reading-dynamics signal.

papers.title: The Role of Lifestyle Medicine in Shaping and Supporting Successful Aging.
papers.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
papers.summary: This perspective proposes a model integrating the six pillars of lifestyle medicine (nutrition, physical activity, stress management, restorative sleep, social connection, and avoidance of risky substances) with principles of successful aging. The model suggests proactive behavioral strategies may foster optimal cognitive and physical functioning and disease prevention in aging.

papers.title: Respiration and individual differences shape behavioral and inter-brain synchronization
papers.summary: In a musical synchronization task with 88 participants and hyperscanning EEG, instructed in-phase and anti-phase breathing increased inter-brain phase-locking and perceived social closeness but reduced behavioral synchrony compared with natural breathing. Inhalation was associated with stronger inter-brain synchronization but less precise behavioral coordination, and partners with faster spontaneous production rates led and showed alpha-band inter-brain phase advance.

papers.title: Diabetes Insipidus as a Rare Complication of Metastatic Breast Cancer With Pituitary Metastases.
papers.summary: A case report describes a patient with metastatic breast cancer and pituitary metastases who presented with central diabetes insipidus, confirmed by hyperosmolar serum, low urine osmolality, and a positive desmopressin challenge. Despite symptomatic relief from desmopressin, the patient deteriorated and died three months after diagnosis, highlighting central DI as a rare but important complication requiring prompt multidisciplinary care.

papers.title: Coblation intracapsular tonsillectomy outcomes in paediatric obstructive sleep disordered breathing: A Singapore study.
papers.journal: Annals of the Academy of Medicine, Singapore
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 102 children undergoing coblation intracapsular tonsillectomy with concurrent adenoidectomy for obstructive sleep-disordered breathing, no post-operative haemorrhage or major complications occurred. Median OSA-18 score improved significantly from 74 to 29.5 at 3 months (P<0.001), with 82.4% having no snoring and mild postoperative pain.

papers.title: Spiritual well-being, sleep quality as a buffer against burnout and in increasing professional fulfillment among healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 661 healthcare professionals in the UAE found that poor sleep quality and irregular circadian patterns were significantly associated with higher burnout, while higher spiritual well-being showed a strong negative correlation with burnout and a positive association with professional fulfillment. Multivariate analysis identified sleep regularity and spiritual well-being as significant independent predictors of both burnout and professional fulfillment.

papers.title: PSYCHONEUROLOGICAL THERAPY FOR POST-COVID SYNDROME: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF METHODS AND CLINICAL EFFECTIVENESS.
papers.summary: This comprehensive review synthesized evidence on psychoneurological therapeutic approaches for post-COVID syndrome, finding consistent support for multiple modalities including SSRIs/SNRIs, cognitive behavioral therapy, physical rehabilitation, complementary therapies, and neuromodulation. The authors conclude that individualized multimodal strategies are most effective for improving cognitive, emotional, and functional outcomes.

papers.title: PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING AMONG MEDICAL STUDENTS AT FIVE UNIVERSITIES IN TBILISI, GEORGIA: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY OF PERCEIVED STRESS, ANXIETY, AND SLEEP QUALITY.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study of 300 medical students in Tbilisi, Georgia, found high prevalence of psychological distress: mean PSS-10 was 26.20 (96.3% moderate-to-high stress), mean GAD-7 was 13.45 (73.7% moderate-to-severe anxiety), and 58.0% reported poor sleep quality. Stress scores were significantly higher in senior years (years 4-6) compared to junior years (years 1-3), with the highest mean in year 6.

papers.title: Effect of early regional anesthesia on postoperative cognitive function and the perioperative stress response in patients with hip fractures: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 76 elderly hip fracture patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty, administering anterior iliopsoas muscle space block (AIMSB) one day before surgery versus one hour before surgery did not significantly reduce the incidence of postoperative delirium (8.1% vs 12.8%; risk difference -4.7%; 95% CI [-18.4% to 9.0%]; P = 0.71). Transient early postoperative pain scores were lower in the day-before group at 6 hours, but differences did not survive multiple comparison correction, and an exploratory IL-6 curve AUC finding requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Navigating the storm: A qualitative research on contributing factors to diabetes burnout in young adults with type 1 diabetes.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: This qualitative content analysis of semi-structured interviews with 11 young adults with type 1 diabetes in Iran identified four interrelated themes contributing to diabetes burnout: disruptions in self-management routines, external stressors and resource limitations, fluctuations in physical and emotional well-being, and the role of interpersonal and social support. These factors were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the need for holistic diabetes care addressing medical and psychosocial dimensions.

papers.title: Tiredness and the Capacity to Decide: The Example of Maternity Care.
papers.summary: This bioethics paper argues that tiredness can impair patients' decision-making capacity, particularly in maternity care where fatigue is common, and therefore justifies testing for capacity in some cases. It contends that recognizing and assessing tiredness in practice is not paternalistic, and that failing to act on this recognition constitutes 'dependency denial' that harms women.

papers.title: Sleep-disordered breathing in children with class II and large overjet treated with removable functional appliance - A longitudinal study.
papers.journal: Cranio : the journal of craniomandibular practice
papers.summary: This longitudinal study examined sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) in children aged 9–14 with class II and large overjet ≥6 mm before, during, and after treatment with a removable functional appliance, compared to controls. At baseline, 8.6% of the study group had SDB versus none in controls, but no significant between-group differences in SDB changes over time were found.

papers.title: One Step at a Time: Design and Rationale for Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trials.
papers.summary: This article presents the design and rationale for stepped-wedge cluster randomized trials, discussing their advantages, limitations, and key considerations for implementation in real-world settings. It highlights the need for statistical analysis that accounts for temporal trends and provides an example of a stepped-wedge study across 26 hospitals evaluating the Eat, Sleep, Console approach for neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome.

papers.title: Determination of the Presence of Daridorexant, a New Hypnotic, in Hair After a Single Exposure and Application to Repetitive Exposures.
papers.summary: This study detected daridorexant in hair after single and repeated exposures using LC-MS/MS, reporting concentrations of 0.029 pg/mg after a single 25-mg dose and 0.8 pg/mg after 6 days of repeated dosing; an assault victim’s hair showed 35 pg/mg after voluntary prescribed use. It provides the first quantitative hair analysis data for daridorexant, highlighting the need for sensitive analytical methods.

papers.title: International Survey of Growth Hormone and Sleep Evaluation Practices in Infants With Prader-Willi Syndrome.
papers.summary: An international survey assessed clinician practices regarding growth hormone (GH) initiation and sleep evaluation in infants with Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS). High-volume clinicians (>21 PWS patients annually) were significantly more likely to report not always performing a baseline polysomnogram before GH initiation compared to low-volume clinicians, primarily to avoid delaying therapy.

papers.title: Characteristics, Risk Factors, and Long-Term Outcomes of Dysphagia Following Modified Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty: A Mixed-Methods Study.
papers.journal: Clinical otolaryngology : official journal of ENT-UK ; official journal of Netherlands Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology & Cervico-Facial Surgery
papers.summary: This prospective mixed-methods study of 120 OSAHS patients undergoing modified uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (mUPPP) found that 63.3% screened positive for dysphagia at 2 weeks postoperatively, with FEES confirming swallowing abnormalities in over 94% of those. Independent risk factors included female gender, GERD, anxiety/depression, and excessive daytime sleepiness; dysphagia persisted in 19.2% at 6 months and 9.2% at 12 months.

papers.title: [One anastomosis mini gastric bypass in patients with severe obesity].
papers.summary: This study evaluated 3-year outcomes of one-anastomosis mini-gastric bypass in 17 patients with severe obesity (median age 47 years, preoperative BMI 64.28 kg/m2), assessing anthropometrics, glucose metabolism, lipid profile, blood pressure, and medication use at multiple postoperative time points. It reported total weight loss of 37.6 kg, excess weight loss of 57.3%, diabetes remission in 84%, regression of sleep apnea symptoms in 94.1%, normal blood pressure or reduced medication need in 50%, and LDL normalization or statin dose reduction in 79%, concluding the procedure is relatively safe with a minimal rate of early postoperative complications.

papers.title: Unpacking the Obesity Paradox in Lung Cancer: A Nationwide Analysis of In-Hospital Mortality From the US National Inpatient Sample (2020-2022).
papers.summary: Using US National Inpatient Sample data from 2020-2022, this retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 61,963 unweighted lung cancer hospitalizations found that documented obesity coding was present in 11.4% and was independently associated with 33% lower odds of in-hospital death (adjusted OR 0.67; 95% CI 0.58-0.77; p<0.001). The authors caution that this association likely reflects confounding by illness severity, reverse causation, and limitations of administrative obesity coding rather than a protective effect of adiposity.

papers.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Pain Chronification: Neuroimmune Rationale, Evidence Boundaries, and Trial Design Priorities: A Structured Narrative Review.
papers.summary: A structured narrative review evaluated cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) as an early, mechanism-informed intervention in pain chronification by synthesizing prespecified evidence domains on neuroimmune/glial mechanisms, brain-network mechanisms, CBT outcomes, and trial design. It found translational support for neuroimmune contributions to central sensitization but insufficient human evidence for direct CBT effects on microglial or astrocytic activation, while CBT showed reproducible small effects on pain intensity and more consistent benefits for interference, disability, distress, coping, sleep, and function, leading the authors to recommend risk-stratified, component-specific, mechanism-embedded trials.

papers.title: A serum cytokine-derived integrated inflammatory profile score (IIPS) links systemic inflammation to symptom burden and severity in COPD.
papers.summary: The study derived an Integrated Inflammatory Profile Score (IIPS) from serum cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2, IL-10) in 62 stable COPD patients, finding it significantly associated with FEV1% predicted (R2=0.1867) and better at discriminating spirometric severity (AUC=0.7381) than individual cytokines. IIPS showed only trend-level associations with symptom domains like sleep and energy, suggesting limited explanatory power for patient-reported burden.

papers.title: A Semi-Dry, Visually Comfortable c-VEP BCI with Short Calibration, Conservative Idle-State Behavior, and a VR Proof of Concept
papers.summary: The paper introduces a usability-oriented code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) brain-computer interface combining low-salience textured stimulation, slow flashing codes, asynchronous evidence accumulation, and semi-dry EEG, and evaluated it in 30 participants on an 11-class keypad typing task plus a VR proof-of-concept shell game. It reported 99.8% keypad accuracy with 33 s calibration and 4.3 s mean decoding time, no spurious commands during a 2-min idle condition, 100% VR accuracy with 5.6 s decoding time, high visual comfort and minimal peripheral distraction in both conditions, and higher fatigue in VR.

papers.title: ASSOCIATION OF PULMONARY AND CUTANEOUS CHANGES IN COVID-19-RELATED CONDITIONS.
papers.summary: This retrospective study examined relationships between COVID-19 severity and maculopapular skin manifestations, assessing lesion area, itching, dryness, pain/discomfort, and peeling alongside CRP, D-dimer, procalcitonin, and oxygen saturation. In the studied patients, moderate and severe SARS-CoV-2 was characterized by maculopapular lesions; rash was generalized in 65.8% (198 patients), involved the bilateral jawline/periauricular area in 77.7% (234), and abdomen in 67.8% (204), with a mean duration of 10.4±2.21 days, and strong correlations were found between alveolar desquamation area and skin lesion area (r=0.73) or peeling (r=0.74), and between skin lesion area and D-dimer (r=0.71) and procalcitonin (r=0.70).

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
